Save the results of a run

Source: R/save_results.R
save_results.Rd

save_results() writes one results object for each scenario and simulation of a run, and stacks the simulations. It checks the fake scenarios with their expect_ functions, and writes no results file when an object fails check_results().

Usage

save_results(r, p, scenarios, gitexclude = NULL)

Arguments

r

The value of run_plan() for the plan p.

p

The plan, with data from add_data() and analyses from add_analyses().

scenarios

The scenarios of the run, from scenarios(). They MUST be the scenarios of the analyses of p.

gitexclude

NULL, or the names of the analysis kinds whose results hold data for each person. See the section Two files.

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame of every assertion, with the columns scenario, assertion, expected, observed and pass.

Details

Call initialize_project() first. For each scenario and simulation, save_results() builds one results object, a named list. Its first element is manifest. When a data function returned a cohort::CohortPipeline, the next element is exclusions, the exclusion tables of the cohorts row-bound in the order of add_data(). The column data names the data of each row. The section A cohort as the data of add_data() gives the columns. A plan without a cohort has no element exclusions. Then comes one element for each analysis kind of add_analyses(), under the kind name and in the order of the calls. The scenario "real" has no element of a kind with control = TRUE. The element of a kind holds the values of its analyses for that scenario and simulation, in the order of the plan:

  • When each value is a data.frame, the element is the values row-bound. Each extra dimension of the kind comes first as a column, unless the data.frame has a column of that name already. A data.table stays a data.table. A kind without extra dimensions has the data.frame of its one analysis.

  • When each value is a list of data.frames with the same names, each name once, the element is a named list with these names. Each of its data.frames is the data.frames of that name row-bound, with the rule of a data.frame above. An example is results$sem$estimates and results$sem$fit.

  • Otherwise, a kind without extra dimensions has the value of its one analysis.

  • Otherwise, the element is a named list with one entry for each analysis. Each name is <name>__<i>, the analysis name without the scenario and the simulation. So the names are the same in each simulation. add_analyses() gives the order of <i>.

The manifest is a list with these elements:

  • pbn_version and r_version.

  • packages, a named character vector. The names are the attached and loaded packages of this R session that are not base packages, and the values are their versions. qs2 is always in the list, because it writes the file. With 2 or more workers of run_plan(), the list also holds the packages loaded on a worker at the end of the run. An example is the package of a model. With 2 or more workers, this R session also loads doFuture and the packages that it imports, such as future, so the list then holds these too.

  • run_date, the date of the call as YYYY-MM-DD. It has no time, so two runs on one day with the same inputs and packages write the same bytes.

  • version, scenario, sim and sims.

  • settings, the named list of the setting columns of the scenario. It is an empty list when there are none.

  • source_md5, the md5 of <version>_run.R and of each file in <version>_functions/ at any depth, also a file that is not an .R file, named by the path relative to home. The one file that it MAY leave out is <version>_functions/blocks.R, the blocks of show_block(). initialize_project() leaves it out only when it cannot change the results, which is when each of these holds:

    • it parses.

    • each top-level expression assigns with <- or = a name to function(...), or blocks to list(...).

    • no other file of the folder assigns one of its names.

    • no other file and no run script uses one of its names.

    Otherwise source_md5 holds it, also when the rule blocks_list of check_project() is warn or off. A change of a blocks file of that shape thus keeps the results current. initialize_project() computes the md5 before it sources the files. The cache key of add_data() holds the md5 of the files data_*.R only, so it never held blocks.R. The rule manifest_source needs the run script in source_md5, so save_results() stops when <version>_run.R did not exist.

  • For the scenario "real" only, data_files, the fingerprint of the files under the folders of folders of initialize_project() when run_plan() started. It is a data.frame with the columns file, size and mtime. Each file is <folder name>/<path in the folder>, for example main/sub/d.csv, and never the path of the folder. pbn reads no content of a data file. The section The fingerprint of the data of initialize_project() gives the rules. So the manifest names the data that the run read, also after a change of a file since initialize_project(). The same files in another place, with the same modification times, give the same manifest. save_results() stops for "real" when a folder did not exist when initialize_project() ran.

  • For the scenario "real" only, fake_real_data, TRUE or FALSE: the argument fake_real_data of initialize_project().

  • For the scenario "real" only, failed_fake_checks, a character vector. It holds each fake scenario of the same call of save_results() with a failed assertion, in the order of scenarios. It is empty when each one passed, or when scenarios has no fake scenario. read_results() stops on real results where it is not empty.

  • For a fake scenario only, fake_md5, one md5 of the code of the data functions of add_data(), without their source references: each fn, and each step of the steps form. A change in a function that fn or a step calls does not change fake_md5. source_md5 holds the md5 of the files of those functions.

  • n_rows_data, a named integer vector with the number of rows of each data element. A list of data.frames with one number of rows, for example a list of imputed data sets, has the rows of one of them. Each other element that is not a data.frame has NA.

  • n_rows_lists, a named list with one entry for each data element that is a list of data.frames with 2 or more numbers of rows. The entry is an integer vector with the rows of each data.frame, in the order of the list. Such an element has NA in n_rows_data. The list is empty when no data element is such a list. The rule no_row_per_person checks each of these numbers. The analysis <scenario>__sim_<kkkk>__pbn_n_rows of add_analyses() counts them where the data is, also on a worker. The rule no_row_per_person reads it.

  • n_rows_before_exclusions, a named integer vector with the number of rows given to the cohort of each data element, or NA for data without a cohort. no_row_per_person reads it too.

  • n_rows_after_exclusions, the same for the rows after the exclusions: n_after of the last step of the exclusion table. It has a number also when n_rows_data is NA, for example for a mids object.

  • analyses, a data.frame with the columns analysis, control and file: the analysis kinds in the object, and the file of each, "results.qs2" or "results_gitexclude.qs2".

  • data_cache, a data.frame with one row for each data element of add_data() and the columns data, cache, from_cache and cache_key. cache is the argument of add_data(). from_cache is TRUE when run_plan() read the data from the cache. cache_key is the md5 of the cache key, or NA without a cache.

save_results() does these steps in this order. It stops at the first step that fails:

  1. It checks its arguments. It stops when r has no stamp of run_plan() for p. It stops when the settings of scenarios are not the settings in the argsets of p. It stops when a fake scenario has no function expect_<scenario>(results) in the environment of initialize_project(), or when an analysis of r failed. In a git repository, it stops when git does not ignore each file that it would write into a folder sims_gitexclude/. The error names the first 3 of the files that git does not ignore. It writes no results file then, and it writes the run log with its error.

  2. It builds every results object, and the stacked object of each scenario with more than 1 simulation, and checks each with check_results(). On a failure, it prints each failed rule with cat(), writes no results file and stops.

  3. When scenarios holds "real", it first replaces the check.csv of "real" with one failed assertion, not checked yet. So read_results() refuses the real results of an earlier run, also when save_results() stops before it writes "real". It does steps 3 and 4 for the fake scenarios first, and then for "real". So the manifest of the real results records each fake scenario of the same run with a failed assertion. The element failed_fake_checks holds them. For each scenario, it replaces check.csv with one failed assertion, not checked yet, so that read_results() refuses the new results until step 4 checks them. It deletes the folders output/ and output_fake_data/ of each scenario that it writes, with one printed line. That output belongs to the results of an earlier run. The section Output of the run log then says that this run made no output, until make_outputs() runs. Then it writes the files of the section The files. The files of the scenarios that are not in scenarios stay as they are.

  4. For each scenario with a function expect_<scenario>(), it calls that function on the results of the scenario. expect_real() is optional. The function MUST return a data.frame with at least one row and the columns assertion, expected, observed and pass. save_results() writes it to <version>_results/<scenario>/check.csv and prints it. For "real" without expect_real(), it deletes check.csv. An error, zero rows or another shape is one failed assertion. A change of an object of the functions folder in place, for example CFG, adds one failed assertion that names the first element that changed. The section on these objects in add_analyses() gives the rules. This rule is the same for expect_real() and for the fake scenarios. save_results() writes check.csv to a temporary file in the same folder and renames it, so a reader never sees a part of it.

  5. It writes the run log <version>_results/run.md, also after a stop in step 2, 3 or 4. The section The run log gives its content.

  6. After every scenario, it stops when a value of pass is not TRUE. It prints each failed assertion in full with cat(), because R cuts an error message at 1000 bytes by default. The error gives the number of failed assertions, their scenarios and the path of check.csv. The files stay, so that you can find the fault, and read_results() stops on them until the assertions pass.

The run log

run_plan() replaces the run log at its start with a short log that says that the run has not finished. A run that ends before the next log, for example when R stops, leaves that log. run_plan() also writes the full log when it stops on failed analyses, and make_outputs() adds its files to it in the same R session. Each run replaces the file, and carries its section History forward. The log is GitHub-flavoured Markdown in ASCII, with these sections in this order:

  • When: the date and the time of the start of the run.

  • Run: the result in one sentence and the scenarios of the run. Then the run date of each other scenario on the disk, from its manifest. Then the versions of R, pbn, plnr and cohort, the number of the other packages, and the number of workers. The manifest of each results file lists the other packages.

  • Failures, only after a failure: the failed analyses with their errors, the number of analyses that did not run after the stop of the run, the failed assertions, and the failed rules of check_results().

  • Scenarios: the simulations and the analyses of each scenario.

  • Data: the cache and the rows of each data element.

  • Exclusions: the exclusion table of simulation 1 of each scenario. A cohort without an exclusion step gets one sentence instead.

  • Assertions: the count for each scenario, and its assertions. For more than 30 assertions, the failed ones only.

  • Output and Files: the files of make_outputs() and the number of warnings of the output function for each scenario, without their text. Then the results files, with their sizes.

  • Timings: seconds on the clock. The wall seconds of each step of the main session, and of each scenario. Then the calls of each data step and analysis kind of each scenario, with the median and the maximum seconds of one call. The share gives its part of the seconds of all data steps and analyses.

  • History: one line for each run of this version, oldest first. Each line gives the start and the result in a few words. It also gives the scenarios, the workers, the wall seconds of run_plan(), save_results() and make_outputs(), and the version of pbn.

The log holds counts, exclusion tables and the rows of check.csv. It never holds the text of an error, because an error message can hold a value of the data. These errors get a number in the log:

  • the error of each failed analysis or data step, one number for each message,

  • the error of an expect_ function that stopped,

  • the detail of each failed rule of check_results(), which can quote a name of the project,

  • the error of save_results() itself, also in the checks of its arguments,

  • the error of the output function of make_outputs().

The file <version>_results/run_errors_gitexclude.md holds the full text of each error under its number. In a git repository, pbn writes it only when git ignores it, as the line *gitexclude* of .gitignore does. Otherwise the log says that the file is missing. Each run deletes the old file, and pbn writes it only when the run has an error.

A project string outside a table, for example a file name of make_outputs(), is on one line as a code span. A string in a table cell is on one line too. So a line end in a string cannot start a heading or a list item.

Only the sections When, Timings and History change in every run. Two runs of the same code on one day, with the same data and cache, give the same other lines. So put run.md in git, and git diff shows the real changes of a run. render_run() renders the log to a PDF.

pbn measures each time with proc.time() in the R session that does the work, also on a worker. A data step gets the time of its function. Data from the cache gets the time of the read. An analysis gets the time of its action function. Each one also records the time of the clock of the computer at its end. A scenario runs from the start of its first data step or analysis to the end of its last one. All workers run on this computer, so their clocks are one clock. With workers, the scenarios overlap, so their seconds do not add up to those of run_plan(). No timing goes to the value of run_plan(), a results file, check.csv or a cache key.

The history is in run.md only. The log at the start of run_plan() adds the line "did not finish" for the run. The full log replaces that line, so each run has one line. A run that R stops keeps its line "did not finish". pbn reads the history from the run.md on the disk. When it cannot read a line, for example after a hand edit, it leaves the line out and prints one line. The run goes on. A deleted run.md starts the history again.

The files

git gets the results of each scenario as one file, results.qs2, and never the results of each simulation. These are the files of <version>_results/<scenario>/:

check.csv                  the assertions of expect_<scenario>()
results.qs2                the results, stacked for more than 1 simulation
results_gitexclude.qs2     the kinds of `gitexclude`, stacked the same way
sims_gitexclude/           only for more than 1 simulation
  sim_<kkkk>.qs2           the results of simulation <kkkk>
  sim_<kkkk>_gitexclude.qs2  the kinds of `gitexclude` of simulation <kkkk>

A scenario with 1 simulation has no folder sims_gitexclude/. Its results.qs2 is the results object of its one simulation. For more simulations, results.qs2 holds the simulations stacked, with the rules of the section Stacking. The name of sims_gitexclude/ holds gitexclude, so the line *gitexclude* of .gitignore keeps it out of git. A clone of the repository thus has no results of one simulation. read_results() with sim reads them.

Before it writes a scenario, save_results() deletes each file in its sims_gitexclude/, and prints one line when there was one. So no simulation of an earlier run stays, for example after sims became smaller. For a scenario that now has 1 simulation, it deletes the folder.

save_results() stops when a file or a folder that it deletes is still there afterwards, for example because another program holds it open on Windows. The error names the file.

pbn 2026.11.22 and older wrote the results of each simulation to sim_<kkkk>/results.qs2, and git tracked them. When save_results() writes a scenario with more than 1 simulation, it deletes each folder sim_<kkkk>/ of that scenario, and prints one line.

Stacking

The stacked results hold every element of the results of simulation 1, in the same order. These rules apply at each depth:

  • A data.frame gets a first column sim, and the rows of the simulations in order. It keeps the class of simulation 1, so a data.table stays a data.table.

  • A list is stacked element by element, and pbn matches the elements by name. So each element of a list MUST have its own name.

  • Each other element becomes a list with one entry for each simulation, named sim_0001, sim_0002 and so on. This includes an atomic vector, a matrix, a factor, a date and NULL.

Stacking stops when two simulations differ in the structure at one path, and the error names the path and the two simulations. It also stops on a data.frame with a column sim, because pbn adds that column.

The manifest is that of simulation 1. In it, sim and n_rows_data are NA, sims is the number of simulations, and stacked is TRUE. The columns from_cache and cache_key of data_cache are NA. The counts n_rows_before_exclusions and n_rows_after_exclusions are NA too, and n_rows_lists is an empty list. The element n_rows_by_sim holds the counts of each simulation. It is a data.frame with one row for each simulation and data element. Its columns are sim, data, n_rows_data, n_rows_before_exclusions and n_rows_after_exclusions. Each data.frame of an entry of n_rows_lists adds a row with the data <element>[[i]] and its rows in n_rows_data. The rule no_row_per_person of check_results() reads it.

Two files

save_results() writes the results of the kinds in gitexclude to results_gitexclude.qs2, beside results.qs2, and to sim_<kkkk>_gitexclude.qs2, beside each sim_<kkkk>.qs2. The section The files shows them. results.qs2 and sim_<kkkk>.qs2 hold manifest, exclusions and every other kind. Use gitexclude for a kind with fitted models, imputations or one row for each person. The project's .gitignore MUST hold the line *gitexclude*, so that git never tracks that file. read_results() reads both files.

These rules apply:

  • save_results() stops before it writes anything when a name in gitexclude is not an analysis kind of p.

  • In a git repository, it also stops when git does not ignore results_gitexclude.qs2.

  • check_results() checks results.qs2 and sim_<kkkk>.qs2, and not the files of gitexclude.

  • The simulations of the two files are stacked apart, with the rules of the section Stacking.

  • Without kinds in gitexclude, save_results() deletes an old results_gitexclude.qs2 of the scenario, and prints one line. The old sim_<kkkk>_gitexclude.qs2 files go with the rest of sims_gitexclude/, see the section The files.

Examples

home <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbn_save_example")
dir.create(file.path(home, "v01_functions"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(home, "data"))
writeLines("extends: house_2026_11_19", file.path(home, "pbn.yml"))
writeLines("# The run script.", file.path(home, "v01_run.R"))
writeLines(
  c(
    "CFG <- list(scenarios = data.frame(scenario = c('real', 'null'), sims = 1))",
    "expect_null <- function(results) {",
    "  data.frame(assertion = 'one row', expected = 1,",
    "    observed = nrow(results$means), pass = nrow(results$means) == 1)",
    "}"
  ),
  file.path(home, "v01_functions", "_cfg.R")
)
env <- new.env()
pbn::initialize_project("v01", home, c(main = file.path(home, "data")), env = env)
#> You are NOT sourcing into .GlobalEnv. All functions will be sourced into an environment that is returned from this function.
#> Sourcing all code inside /tmp/Rtmp2kjTOx/pbn_save_example/v01_functions into 

scenarios <- pbn::scenarios(env$CFG)
p <- plnr::Plan$new()
pbn::add_data(p, "d", fn = function(scenario, sim) {
  return(data.frame(x = stats::rnorm(5)))
})
pbn::add_analyses(p, scenarios, name = "means", fn = function(data, argset) {
  return(data.frame(mean_x = mean(data$d$x)))
})
r <- pbn::run_plan(p)
pbn::save_results(r, p, scenarios)
#> Assertions of the scenario "null":
#>  assertion expected observed pass
#>    one row        1        1 TRUE
#> pbn: wrote the run log v01_results/run.md.
names(pbn::read_results("v01", home = home))
#> [1] "manifest" "means"   

unlink(home, recursive = TRUE)
